verses.text: Family of Israel, listen to what the LORD’s telling you!
The LORD says, “Don’t pick up the ways of the nations. Don’t panic over signs in the sky just because those nations do.
The customs those people follow are empty. Someone cuts a tree from the forest, and a craftsman shapes it with an ax.
They dress it up in silver and gold, then hammer in nails to keep it from moving.
Their idols are like palms someone carved. They can’t talk, and people have to carry them because they can’t move. Don’t be scared of them. They can’t hurt you, and they can’t help you either.”
Nobody’s like you, LORD. You’re great, and your name is great in power.
Who could fail to fear you, King of the nations? That honor belongs to you. Look through every nation’s wise people and all their royal courts. There’s nobody like you.
They’re all senseless and foolish, taking lessons from idols. It’s just wood!
They bring beaten sheets of silver from Tarshish and gold from Uphaz. An engraver and a goldsmith do the work. They dress the idols in blue and purple. Every one is made by skilled hands.
The LORD is the true God. He’s the living God and the King forever. The earth shudders when he’s angry. The nations can’t stand up to his fury.
“Here’s what you’ll tell them: ‘The gods that never made the sky or the earth will disappear off the earth and out from under the sky.’”
God made the earth by his power. He set the world in place by his wisdom and stretched the heavens out by his understanding.
When he speaks, the waters in the sky roar. He sends mist rising from the far ends of the earth. He makes lightning for the rain and brings the wind out of his storehouses.
People have become senseless and clueless. Every goldsmith is let down by the idol they’ve carved. The image they cast is a lie. There’s no breath in it.
They’re useless, the product of a lie. When their time of reckoning comes, they’ll be gone.
Jacob’s God, the one who’s his share, is nothing like those idols. He made everything, and Israel is the tribe he keeps as his own inheritance. The LORD of Armies is his name.
You who live under siege, pack up your belongings and get them out of the land.
The LORD says, “Watch. This time I’m going to sling the people out of the land. I’ll bring trouble down on them so they feel it.”
I’m in agony over this injury! My wound is serious, but I said, “This really is my grief, and I have to carry it.”
My tent is wrecked and all the ropes have snapped. My children have left me and are gone. There’s nobody left to stretch out my tent or hang its curtains again.
The shepherds have become senseless. They never asked the LORD what to do. So they’ve gotten nowhere, and all their flocks have scattered.
Listen, news is coming! There’s a huge uproar out of the north. It’ll leave the towns of Judah deserted, a place for jackals to live.
LORD, I know we don’t set our own course in life. A person walking can’t direct their own steps.
LORD, correct me gently. If you do it in anger, you’ll cut me down to nothing.

Pour your fury out on the nations that don’t know you and on the families that don’t call on your name. They’ve devoured Jacob. Yes, they’ve swallowed him up and destroyed him, and they’ve wrecked the place he called home.
